proof:
For $z\in E$, the conditional hyperplane fraction of $\mu_{\ell,z}$ is at most $\eta_\ell/(\mu_{\ell,z}(\mathrm{total})/T_\ell)\to0$. Thus its positive sampled fine bases eventually affinely span $\mathbb R^r$, since otherwise one hyperplane contains all positive mass. In $s\ge1$, a positive-volume sampled section supplies all vertical directions, and the sampled bases span the quotient. In $s=0$ the bases already span the coarse ambient space. In both cases the coarse convex fiber is full dimensional.

Use 77d36834ea2179e7 in dimensions $(r,s)$ to give this one body a block affine map with uniform inner and outer radius bounds. Its geometric normalization holds for any body regardless of the lattice. Dilation by the inverse $m$th root of the image volume gives volume one and preserves universal positive inner and finite outer radius bounds. Write the resulting map as $(u,x)\mapsto(Au+t,Bu+Cx+c)$. It has $|\det A||\det C|=1/M_{\ell,z}$, takes the fine coset to $A(a_\ell+L_\ell)+t$, and the product of its transformed covolume and continuous section Jacobian is exactly $v_\ell/M_{\ell,z}$. Counting at $s=0$ has section Jacobian one. The conditional hyperplane fractions are unchanged, so the quantitative mesh bound gives $\rho(AL_\ell)\to0$ in the bounded normalized body.

A measurable Voronoi fundamental cell of $AL_\ell$ lies in the cube of radius $\rho=\rho(AL_\ell)$. By the one-body estimate in e4ef1ac154c5d280, for a bounded image in a box of radius $R$ the fine sampling error is at most $2r\rho(2R+2\rho)^{m-1}$, uniformly in the coset offset. Thus the weighted fine mass in the normalized body tends to its volume one. The exact product identity gives $\mu_{\ell,z}(\mathrm{total})/M_{\ell,z}\to1$ and then $M_{\ell,z}/T_\ell\to\alpha_z$.

Given $j=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i$ as in the statement, all source fibers are nonempty eventually. Their anchored Minkowski combination lies in $(C_\ell)_j$ by convexity, so $j\in P$. Fix one $i$, choose one point in every other source fiber, and use the resulting translated copy of $\lambda_i(C_\ell)_{z_i}$ contained in $(C_\ell)_j$. In the block linear frame of the source $z_i$, translate this copy to the bounded homothetic image of its volume-one normalized body. The fine coset is then translated, with the same lattice, same covolume and same $\rho\to0$. Its volume is $\lambda_i^m$, and the exact sampled-mass multiplier stays $1/M_{\ell,z_i}$. The same sampling bound and inclusion give $\mu_{\ell,j}(\mathrm{total})\ge M_{\ell,z_i}(\lambda_i^m-o(1))$. Divide by $T_\ell$ to conclude that $\alpha_j\ge\lambda_i^m\alpha_{z_i}>0$. This proves lattice completeness before using any volume limit at $j$. The full Minkowski inclusion and Brunn–Minkowski yield $M_{\ell,j}^{1/m}\ge\sum_i\lambda_iM_{\ell,z_i}^{1/m}$. Divide by $T_\ell^{1/m}$ and pass to the established limits. The sum of the $\alpha_z$ on $E$ is one. The retained coarse mass is therefore asymptotic to $T_\ell$, and the omitted fine mass, which is $o(T_\ell)$, is $o(M_{\ell,E})$.

For each dependence component choose one anchor $z\in E$. Rescale the linear part of its volume-one block map by $(M_{\ell,z}/M_{\ell,E})^{1/m}$. This gives absolute determinant $1/M_{\ell,E}$, stays uniformly round up to translation, and preserves mesh vanishing since the factor tends to $\alpha_z^{1/m}>0$. Every body in that component, under the same map, has volume $M_{\ell,w}/M_{\ell,E}$ bounded away from zero and at most one. Their compatibility is preserved by the common linear map. The anchor-to-component diameter propagation in the proof of aa4df3d20ca63976 uses only a bounded starting diameter and those volume bounds, so it applies starting with this anchor. This gives the claimed common maps. The representation-preserving translations used in a full-shape lift only translate the residual fine cosets.

statement:
Let $k\ge0$, $r\ge1$, $s\ge0$, $m=r+s$. Let $C_\ell\subset\mathbb R^k_z\times\mathbb R^r_u\times\mathbb R^s_x$ be compact convex sets whose nonempty coarse integer fibers have indices in a fixed finite $P\subset\mathbb Z^k$. Sample $u$ in a full-rank lattice coset $a_\ell+L_\ell$ of covolume $v_\ell$. At each coarse site $z$ let $\mu_{\ell,z}$ sum $v_\ell$ times the $s$-volume of its fine sections, using counting for $s=0$. Put $\mu_\ell=\sum_z\mu_{\ell,z}$ and $T_\ell=\mu_\ell(\mathrm{total})>0$. Assume that the largest fraction $\eta_\ell$ of $\mu_\ell$ on an affine hyperplane in the $u$ coordinates tends to zero.

Along any subsequence on which $\mu_{\ell,z}(\mathrm{total})/T_\ell\to\alpha_z$ at every $z$, let $E=\{z:\alpha_z>0\}$ and $M_{\ell,z}=|(C_\ell)_z|_m$. For each $z\in E$, the coarse fiber is eventually a full $m$-body,
$$
\frac{\mu_{\ell,z}(\mathrm{total})}{M_{\ell,z}}\to1,\qquad
\frac{M_{\ell,z}}{T_\ell}\to\alpha_z.
$$
The set $E$ is lattice-complete. For every integer combination point $j=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i$ with $z_i\in E$, $\lambda_i>0$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$, it satisfies
$$
\alpha_j\ge\lambda_i^m\alpha_{z_i}>0\quad\text{for each }i,\qquad
\alpha_j^{1/m}\ge\sum_i\lambda_i\alpha_{z_i}^{1/m}.
$$
In particular $M_{\ell,E}=\sum_{z\in E}M_{\ell,z}\sim T_\ell$ and the fine mass off $E$ is $o(M_{\ell,E})$. Each retained fiber admits a uniformly round volume-one block normalization with transformed fine covering radius tending to zero. On each dependence component of $E$ one can choose a common block map of absolute determinant $1/M_{\ell,E}$ with transformed fine covering radius tending to zero and uniformly bounded diameters of all images in the component.
title: Fine hyperplane nonconcentration yields dense retained components and mass recovery
